 Police arrest man for alleged Benjamin Street home invasion 
 by 
 Dominic Apap 
 November 1, 2026 November 1, 2026 
 Share this:
 Share on X (Opens in new window) 
 X 
 Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) 
 Facebook 
 File Photo/DAILY. Buy this photo. 
 Ypsilanti resident Olin Thurman, 34, was arrested by the Ann Arbor Police Department earlier this week for allegedly breaking into and stealing items from a house on the 500 block of Benjamin Street.
 Investigators believe Thurman entered the house, located near the Intramural Sports Building and Wolverine Village, through an unlocked door on Oct. 24 while occupants were sleeping. The occupants reported the burglary when they woke up. Officers identified and arrested Thurman two days later, recovering stolen items and electronic devices .
 Thurman was arraigned Wednesday and charged with one count of first-degree home invasion and two counts of obstructing a police officer. He was given a $20,000 bond.
 In December of last year, Thurman pleaded guilty to a felony assault charge, according to court records.
 In a statement on Facebook, the AAPD recommended taking precautionary measures to prevent home invasions.
 “We want to remind community members of the importance of locking all doors and windows before going to sleep,” the statement read. “Community members are also urged to call 911 if they ever see anything suspicious.”
 Daily News Editor Dominic Apap can be reached at dapap@umich.edu .
